hints.S02_A1: The dash spells out the clues: ROUND, SOFT and perfectly still, and the puppy is compared to a CLOUD. Ask: which word describes something light and soft like a cloud - not its colour, not its noise, not how hard it feels?
hints.S02_A2: A happy DOG moves its TAIL from side to side, and English has one special verb for exactly that. Ask: does a dog shake, pull or break its tail when its OWNER comes home, or does it do that friendly side-to-side movement?
hints.S02_A3: Nina brings the STRAY cat INSIDE before the heavy RAIN - this is kindness, not escape. Ask: which choice means to take care of something? Two choices mean abandoning it and one means forcing your way in.
hints.S02_A4: Biscuit is found ALIVE and well after she had been so WORRIED. Ask: does this idiom describe great happiness and relief, or illness, or trouble, or confusion? An idiom cannot be read word by word - match it to the feeling.
hints.S02_A5: Father forgot to CLEAN the fish TANK for three WEEKS. Ask: what happens to water nobody cleans - does it become brighter and clearer, or the opposite? Choose the word that is the opposite of clean, not one about light or space.
hints.S02_B1: The subject is NOBODY, not 'the neighbourhood'. Words like nobody, everybody and someone behave like ONE person. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb, or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S02_B2: 'HAS' is already sitting there, so the blank must be the form that partners with has. Ask: after has, do we use the -ing form, the plain verb, or the past participle? And remember a verb never takes a plural -s.
hints.S02_B3: Two clues: the subject BIRDS is plural, and 'EVERY year' means it happens again and again. Ask: is this a finished past event or a present habit? A plural subject in the present takes the verb with NO -s.
hints.S02_B4: The word THAN gives it away - one animal is being measured against one other. Ask: do we need the plain adjective, the -est form used for three or more, or the comparing form? Never stack 'more' on top of an -er word.
hints.S02_B5: 'THIS MORNING' is already over, so the sentence is past - and 'EAT' after the blank is the plain verb, so the blank must be the helping verb. Ask: which helping verb makes a past negative in front of a plain verb?
hints.S02_B6: A question tag mirrors the main verb: the statement uses ARE, and CATS and dogs is plural. Ask: if the statement is positive, must the tag be positive or negative? And must the tag agree with a plural subject?
hints.S02_B7: CLIMBING needs a helping verb in front of it, and ARRIVED tells you the time is past. Ask: is the MONKEY one animal or many? Match a PAST helping verb to a singular subject - a present form or a plural form breaks the sentence.
hints.S02_B8: KEPT is the verb that decides everything. Ask: after keep or kept, does the next verb appear as the plain form, the -s form, the past form, or the -ing form? Only one verb carries the tense, and KEPT is already doing that job.
hints.S02_C1: The verb WATCHED controls this blank: 'We WATCHED a sea otter ___ in a big tank.' Ask: after watch, see or hear plus an object, does the next verb take -s, -ed, -ing, or nothing at all? The otter being singular does not matter here.
hints.S02_C2: Look at KEPT: 'It KEPT ___ in circles.' Ask: after keep or kept, which single form always follows - the plain verb, the -s form, the past form, or the -ing form? KEPT is already carrying the past tense.
hints.S02_C3: The SIGN on the glass SAYS - says is present, so this blank is present too, and 'this otter' is ONE animal. Ask: in the present tense, does a singular subject take the plain verb or the verb ending in -s?
hints.S02_C4: 'LAST WINTER' is finished time, so this verb must be past - not present, not -ing. Ask: what is the past form of the verb meaning to move through water? It is irregular, so it never takes -ed.
hints.S02_C5: The story is past here: a fish DARTED past and the otter QUICKLY ___ it. Ask: which past form fits? This verb is irregular, so 'catched' does not exist - and the -s form is only for present habits.
hints.S02_C6: 'An OTTER ALWAYS ___ its food with its front paws.' ALWAYS signals a general truth in the present, and 'an otter' is one otter. Ask: present tense plus a singular subject - which ending must the verb carry?
hints.S02_C7: KEPT turns up a second time: 'The hungry otter KEPT ___ more fish.' Ask: if KEPT already shows the past, can the verb after it be past as well? Which form must follow keep or kept, every single time?
hints.S02_C8: 'We waited to SEE it ___ one last fish.' Ask: after see, watch or hear plus an object, which form comes next - the base verb, or one with -s, -ed or -ing? This is the very same rule as blank 1 in this passage.
hints.S02_D1: The clue comes right after the blank: it could FIT INSIDE her PALM. Ask: is this word about size, about character, or about noise? Choose the one that means extremely small.
hints.S02_D2: A STRAY CAT is the one acting, and the bird ends up INJURED with a hurt wing. Ask: did the cat save the bird or run after it across the grass? The blank follows 'had', so a past verb form is needed.
hints.S02_D3: The bird TRIED to FLAP away from Mia - it is trying to escape her. Ask: does escaping show fear or shock? Pick the feeling word that pairs with 'of': you are ___ OF something.
hints.S02_D4: A wildlife OFFICER is called and comes AT ONCE to help the trembling bird. Ask: after 'to', do we need a past verb or a base verb? And does an officer hunt an injured bird, or save it from danger?
hints.S02_D5: The SHELTER protects the bird FROM CATS and cars until its wing has healed. Ask: which box word means 'out of danger'? Watch the pairing - this one goes with FROM, while a different box word goes with 'of'.
hints.S02_F1: This is a yes/no question turned into REPORTED speech. Ask three things: which small joining word follows ASKED? Does the question keep its question word order, or become a normal statement order? And what must happen to 'you' and to 'have'?
hints.S02_F2: BOTH Maya and her brother means TWO people, so your subject is now plural. Ask: does a plural subject keep the -s on the verb, or drop it? And say 'a pet rabbit' only once - do not repeat the whole second sentence.
hints.S02_E1: The class travelled by bus LAST WEEK, so this verb must be past. Ask: does GO build its past by adding -ed, or does it change into a completely different word? Irregular verbs never take -ed.
hints.S02_E2: The underlined word means 'at this place', but the sentence is about BIRDSONG reaching your EARS. Ask: which spelling belongs to your ears? One of them contains the word EAR - that is your clue.
hints.S02_E3: TELL is irregular, so the -ed ending is wrong here. Ask: how do you say it in the past - 'yesterday he ___ us'? It changes its vowel, exactly like sell becomes sold.
hints.S02_E4: Find the subject: SOME ANIMALS, which is more than one. Ask: does a plural subject take the verb with -s, or the verb without it? The -s ending belongs to singular subjects, like 'the animal eats'.
hints.S02_E5: The REPORT belongs to the park rangers - more than one ranger. Ask: does a plain -s show ownership, or does it only make a plural? Where does the apostrophe go when the owners are many?
